effect: The cell has divided into two unspecialized daughter cells, each with a complete genome, completing the chapter.
reaction: The final illustration plan ties division to self-renewal and possible later specialization, though it does not show how gene-use changes produce different paths.

mostWorthwhile.text: Growing the cell before division was most worthwhile: the vesicle-fusion and growth sequence makes clear that daughters receive newly built cellular material, not just halves of the original contents.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle felt comparatively thin: the picture shows fibres, but the result gives little explanation of how they attach to and move chromosomes.

surprise.text: The explicit separation of chromosome distribution from the formation of two nuclei and two cells sharpened my understanding of division.

arbitrary.text: Combining the enlarged cell body with chromosome sets felt a little abstract, even though the matching outlines explain that these are views of the same cell.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter: the staged illustration plans make biological processes understandable, and I am curious how the unspecialized descendants develop different roles.
